pages.title: Nobody Reports the Misses: Counting False Passes in AI for Regulated Work
CrossSource: measuring whether a RAG system can be trusted to cite the law

overrides.s0-stats: Corpus: 22 opinions. Golden set: 25 questions. Retrieval: BM25, top 5. Judge validated: 15 out of 15.
overrides.s2-list: Corpus: 22 public-domain U S court opinions, 16 Supreme Court, 2 federal circuit and 4 state, sourced from Harvard Law School's Caselaw Access Project and chunked to about 350 words. Retrieval: BM25, top 5. Generation: Claude, with mandatory inline citations in doc ID, colon, chunk ID format. Golden set: 25 human-authored questions with verified ground-truth supporting chunks. Two configurations: baseline, which is citation formatting only, versus strict, which adds explicit citation-discipline rules to the prompt. Scoring: claim-level citation precision and recall, faithfulness, and answer relevance, scored by an LLM judge and validated by hand.
overrides.s3-table1: Table 1, baseline versus strict. Citation precision: 0.981 in baseline, 0.994 in strict. Citation recall: 0.760 in both. Faithfulness: 1.000 in both. Answer relevance: 0.980 in baseline, 0.960 in strict.
overrides.s3-table2: Table 2, failure taxonomy by configuration. Right document, wrong passage: 3 in baseline, 1 in strict. Missing authority: 6 in both. Wrong document: 0 in both. Unsupported claim: 0 in both.
overrides.s5-list: Instrument the pipeline. Build a failure taxonomy instead of a single score. Validate the judge externally. Separate precision from recall, so you know whether to fix prompting or retrieval.
overrides.s6-list: Retrieval ablations. Cross-model judge comparison. Law-trained annotation review. Per-question difficulty stratification. An agent-eval module, in build.
